subject: URGENT: FinEdge production retry storm after model-v2.3 quant change
messages:
From: Alicia Hernandez <alicia.hernandez@finedge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@finedge.com
Date: 2026-08-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production 429/503 spike after model v2.3 push - urgent

Team,

We just saw a sudden spike in 429s and 503s across our /generate endpoint starting ~09:05 PDT after the v2.3 quantized model was promoted to prod. Traffic is normal; latency climbed and client SDKs started retrying which has further amplified the problem. Our ops dashboards show request-level retries and a retry loop signature from a subset of short-lived requests.

Attached a short trace sample and a screenshot of the SLO burn rate. Can you confirm if the v2.3 rollout included any kernel-level changes or new quant profiles? This is impacting our checkout flows — escalating internally.

--
Alicia Hernandez
CTO, FinEdge
Alicia.Hernandez@finedge.com

Attachments: traces_sample.jsonl (trace snippet), slo_screenshot.png

- Marissa: I'll coordinate comms and credits; keep FinEdge PM in the loop.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll move quickly.

jordan_blake@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-23T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production 429/503 spike after model v2.3 push - urgent

Quick triage notes:
- Symptoms: sharp rise in 429s and 503s concentrated on requests with short prompt lengths (<= 64 tokens). Autoscaling appears healthy; GPU utilization is moderate.
- Correlation: errors started immediately after the quantized v2.3 kernel switched on for the high-throughput pool. Error traces show frequent KV cache misses followed by synchronous full-context recompute which triggers client retries.
- Hypothesis: a quant-kernel/attention-matmul mismatch for short sequences causes per-request stalls; clients' retry logic compounds the load (retry storm).

Attached: a small trace sample (from Alicia) and a quick metric dump. I recommend an immediate rollback of the v2.3 quant profile for the affected pool back to the v2.2 profile and a canary in a separate pool before reintroducing.

If Jordan/Marissa agree, we can begin the rollback now (should be low-risk, config-level). I'll coordinate the rollback window.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: traces_sample.jsonl
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-23T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production 429/503 spike after model v2.3 push - urgent

Agree with Karthik. Root cause looks like a kernel selection path incorrectly preferring a new fused matmul kernel for short sequence lengths when run with the v2.3 quant table; that path exposes a timing regression and KV cache invalidation edge case.

Immediate action: do a targeted rollback of the quant profile for the high-throughput pool to the v2.2 profile. Steps:
1) Take a single high-throughput instance out of LB.
2) Update quant profile config to v2.2 and reload.
3) Run a fast smoke test against short-seq synthetic workload.
4) Reintroduce and monitor error rate for 20 minutes.

I attached a brief rollback plan (rollback_plan_v1.md). Estimated time to first traffic recovery: 8-12 minutes once we start.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Engineering recommends an immediate rollback to the v2.2 quant profile for that pool; expected recovery in ~10 minutes post-rollback.

Customer impact: checkout flows intermittently failing, increased SLO burn, customer-facing ops alerted and internal execs watching.

Requested support from leadership: please be prepared to approve a one-week credit as compensation and to join a 1-hour postmortem with the FinEdge technical team if leadership requests. I'll keep you posted — rolling now.

-Jordan
